chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who shortens in his estate. He said: There is no problem so long as he has not intended to stay for ten days, unless he has a residence there which he takes as a homeland. I said: What is residence-settlement? He said: That he has a residence there in which he stays for six months; then when that is so, he performs in full there whenever he enters it.

key_terms.الِاسْتِيطَانُ: establishing residence or settlement in a place
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: staying or intending residence for a period
key_terms.سِتَّةَ أَشْهُرٍ: six months, the period mentioned for settlement
key_terms.ضَيْعَتِهِ: his estate, property, or cultivated land
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: ten days, the threshold for a legal stay in this ruling
key_terms.يَسْتَوْطِنُهُ: he takes it as a place of settled residence
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he performs the prayer in full
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: he shortens the prayer while traveling

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler pray in full at his estate or place of residence?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the prayer of a traveler when entering his agricultural property or estate. It explains that he shortens the prayer unless he intends a ten-day stay, but if he has a dwelling there that counts as a place of settlement by residing in it for six months, he performs the prayer in full whenever he enters it.
